documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: restart cadence

The ledger reconciler is restarted every 90 minutes. The cadence is set in the fleet console and applies to every region the ledger reconciler runs in.

## why the cadence is what it is

A restart drains the in-flight queue first, so a shorter cadence costs throughput and a longer one lets memory drift accumulate. 90 minutes is the value the operations team settled on after the last capacity review.

## changing it

Raise a change request before altering the cadence. A restart cadence below 20 minutes needs sign-off, because the drain step alone takes several minutes.

documents.title: ledger reconciler: retry policy
documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: retry policy

The ledger reconciler retries a failed downstream call 8 times before it gives up and marks the work item as failed.

## backoff

Retries are spaced by an exponential backoff starting at 8 seconds. The retry policy is shared by every worker in the ledger reconciler pool, so a downstream outage produces a burst of retries across the whole pool.

## what is not retried

A rejected payload is never retried. The ledger reconciler treats a schema rejection as terminal and routes the item to the dead letter queue.

documents.title: ledger reconciler: alerting threshold
documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: alerting threshold

The ledger reconciler pages the on-call engineer when its backlog passes 200 items.

## how the threshold is measured

Backlog depth is sampled once a minute and the alert fires on three consecutive samples above 200, which keeps a single spike from waking anybody up.

## secondary alerts

A warning is raised at half the paging threshold. The warning goes to the team channel and does not page. Both alerts carry the ledger reconciler service name in their title.

documents.title: ledger reconciler: storage layout
documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: storage layout

The ledger reconciler writes to 4 partitions, keyed by the shipment identifier.

## retention

Each partition keeps 60 days of history and then rolls off. Restoring a rolled-off partition means reading the cold archive, which is a slow path.

## layout on disk

Partitions are laid out one directory per partition, and the ledger reconciler opens every one of them at start-up, so the partition count is also a file descriptor budget.

documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: deployment steps

A release of the ledger reconciler ships through 3 stages before it reaches production traffic.

## the stages

Each stage runs the same smoke suite against a larger slice of traffic. A stage that fails the suite halts the release and the ledger reconciler stays on the previous build.

## rollback

Rollback is one command and skips the intermediate stages, because a rollback target has already passed them once.

documents.title: ledger reconciler: failure modes
documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: failure modes

The failure the ledger reconciler hits most often is a expired credential.

## how it shows up

A expired credential shows up first as a flat processing rate with no error log entries, which is why the ledger reconciler runbook starts at the rate graph rather than at the logs.

## recovery

Recovery is a restart in most cases. A expired credential that survives a restart means the state store is involved and the incident is escalated.

documents.title: ledger reconciler: capacity limit
documents.text:
# ledger reconciler: capacity limit

The ledger reconciler sustains 40 requests a second at the measured steady state.

## headroom

The capacity limit is a measurement rather than a configured cap. Beyond 40 requests a second the ledger reconciler queues rather than rejecting, so the symptom of overload is latency and not an error.

## scaling

Adding workers raises the limit close to linearly until the state store saturates.

The failure the tariff archiver hits most often is a orphaned lock.

## how it shows up

A orphaned lock shows up first as a flat processing rate with no error log entries, which is why the tariff archiver runbook starts at the rate graph rather than at the logs.

## recovery

Recovery is a restart in most cases. A orphaned lock that survives a restart means the state store is involved and the incident is escalated.

documents.title: tariff archiver: capacity limit
documents.text:
# tariff archiver: capacity limit

The tariff archiver sustains 250 requests a second at the measured steady state.

## headroom

The capacity limit is a measurement rather than a configured cap. Beyond 250 requests a second the tariff archiver queues rather than rejecting, so the symptom of overload is latency and not an error.

## scaling

Adding workers raises the limit close to linearly until the state store saturates.

# tariff reconciler: restart cadence

The tariff reconciler is restarted every 240 minutes. The cadence is set in the fleet console and applies to every region the tariff reconciler runs in.

## why the cadence is what it is

A restart drains the in-flight queue first, so a shorter cadence costs throughput and a longer one lets memory drift accumulate. 240 minutes is the value the operations team settled on after the last capacity review.

## changing it

Raise a change request before altering the cadence. A restart cadence below 20 minutes needs sign-off, because the drain step alone takes several minutes.

documents.title: tariff reconciler: retry policy
documents.text:
# tariff reconciler: retry policy

The tariff reconciler retries a failed downstream call 8 times before it gives up and marks the work item as failed.

## backoff

Retries are spaced by an exponential backoff starting at 30 seconds. The retry policy is shared by every worker in the tariff reconciler pool, so a downstream outage produces a burst of retries across the whole pool.

## what is not retried

A rejected payload is never retried. The tariff reconciler treats a schema rejection as terminal and routes the item to the dead letter queue.

documents.title: tariff reconciler: alerting threshold
documents.text:
# tariff reconciler: alerting threshold

The tariff reconciler pages the on-call engineer when its backlog passes 2500 items.

## how the threshold is measured

Backlog depth is sampled once a minute and the alert fires on three consecutive samples above 2500, which keeps a single spike from waking anybody up.

## secondary alerts

A warning is raised at half the paging threshold. The warning goes to the team channel and does not page. Both alerts carry the tariff reconciler service name in their title.

documents.title: tariff reconciler: storage layout
documents.text:
# tariff reconciler: storage layout

The tariff reconciler writes to 16 partitions, keyed by the shipment identifier.

## retention

Each partition keeps 30 days of history and then rolls off. Restoring a rolled-off partition means reading the cold archive, which is a slow path.

## layout on disk

Partitions are laid out one directory per partition, and the tariff reconciler opens every one of them at start-up, so the partition count is also a file descriptor budget.

A release of the invoice planner ships through 3 stages before it reaches production traffic.

## the stages

Each stage runs the same smoke suite against a larger slice of traffic. A stage that fails the suite halts the release and the invoice planner stays on the previous build.

## rollback

Rollback is one command and skips the intermediate stages, because a rollback target has already passed them once.

documents.title: invoice planner: failure modes
documents.text:
# invoice planner: failure modes

The failure the invoice planner hits most often is a truncated upload.

## how it shows up

A truncated upload shows up first as a flat processing rate with no error log entries, which is why the invoice planner runbook starts at the rate graph rather than at the logs.

## recovery

Recovery is a restart in most cases. A truncated upload that survives a restart means the state store is involved and the incident is escalated.

documents.title: invoice planner: capacity limit
documents.text:
# invoice planner: capacity limit

The invoice planner sustains 900 requests a second at the measured steady state.

## headroom

The capacity limit is a measurement rather than a configured cap. Beyond 900 requests a second the invoice planner queues rather than rejecting, so the symptom of overload is latency and not an error.

## scaling

Adding workers raises the limit close to linearly until the state store saturates.

documents.title: invoice indexer: restart cadence
documents.text:
# invoice indexer: restart cadence

The invoice indexer is restarted every 120 minutes. The cadence is set in the fleet console and applies to every region the invoice indexer runs in.

## why the cadence is what it is

A restart drains the in-flight queue first, so a shorter cadence costs throughput and a longer one lets memory drift accumulate. 120 minutes is the value the operations team settled on after the last capacity review.

## changing it

Raise a change request before altering the cadence. A restart cadence below 20 minutes needs sign-off, because the drain step alone takes several minutes.

documents.title: invoice indexer: retry policy
documents.text:
# invoice indexer: retry policy

The invoice indexer retries a failed downstream call 6 times before it gives up and marks the work item as failed.

## backoff

Retries are spaced by an exponential backoff starting at 30 seconds. The retry policy is shared by every worker in the invoice indexer pool, so a downstream outage produces a burst of retries across the whole pool.

## what is not retried

A rejected payload is never retried. The invoice indexer treats a schema rejection as terminal and routes the item to the dead letter queue.

documents.title: invoice indexer: alerting threshold
documents.text:
# invoice indexer: alerting threshold

The invoice indexer pages the on-call engineer when its backlog passes 2500 items.

## how the threshold is measured

Backlog depth is sampled once a minute and the alert fires on three consecutive samples above 2500, which keeps a single spike from waking anybody up.

## secondary alerts

A warning is raised at half the paging threshold. The warning goes to the team channel and does not page. Both alerts carry the invoice indexer service name in their title.

documents.title: invoice indexer: storage layout
documents.text:
# invoice indexer: storage layout

The invoice indexer writes to 4 partitions, keyed by the shipment identifier.

## retention

Each partition keeps 14 days of history and then rolls off. Restoring a rolled-off partition means reading the cold archive, which is a slow path.

## layout on disk

Partitions are laid out one directory per partition, and the invoice indexer opens every one of them at start-up, so the partition count is also a file descriptor budget.

Read access to the invoice indexer dashboards is open to every engineer. Write access is granted through the group and reviewed each quarter.
